overview: LSEG is a global, multi-asset-class financial markets infrastructure (FMI) and data provider operating across the entire trade lifecycle, from pre-trade data and analytics through execution, clearing and post-trade services. Formed from the 2021 acquisition of Refinitiv (and the earlier purchase of FTSE Russell/LCH), the Group now comprises four divisions -- Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell, Risk Intelligence and Markets (including Tradeweb and LCH clearing) -- serving customers in over 170 countries. The business is highly cash-generative and over 70% recurring/subscription in nature, giving it a defensive, 'all-weather' revenue profile that is uncorrelated to any single macro factor.

business_model.summary: LSEG monetises its position across the trade lifecycle through subscriptions to data, analytics and index products (Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell, Risk Intelligence) combined with transactional/volume-linked revenue from trading venues and clearing (Markets, including Tradeweb and LCH). Over 70% of group income is recurring; the remainder is transactional and benefits from volatility and rising trading volumes, making the overall model resilient through the cycle.

revenue_streams.name: Data & Analytics
revenue_streams.detail: Workflows (Workspace, ~48% of divisional revenue), Data & Feeds (~46%), Analytics (~6%); 98% recurring. FY2025 organic growth +5.8% (Workflows +3.1%, Data & Feeds +6.6%, Analytics +7.7%); H1 2026 organic growth accelerated to +5.1%

revenue_streams.name: Markets
revenue_streams.detail: Equities, Fixed Income/Tradeweb, FX, OTC Derivatives (SwapClear/LCH), Securities & Reporting, Non-Cash Collateral, Net Treasury Income; 59% transactional. FY2025 organic growth +11.6% in OTC Derivatives, +13.7% in Fixed Income/Tradeweb; H1 2026 organic growth +11.9%, the fastest-growing division

revenue_streams.name: FTSE Russell
revenue_streams.detail: 100% recurring; Subscriptions ~66%, Asset-based (ETF/index-linked AUM) fees ~34%. FY2025 organic growth +7.3%; H1 2026 +9.1%. AUM in ETFs linked to FTSE Russell indices reached $2 trillion in H1 2026

revenue_streams.name: Risk Intelligence
revenue_streams.detail: World-Check screening, Digital Identity & Fraud, due diligence; 78% recurring. FY2025 organic growth +11.7% (double-digit); H1 2026 +9.7%

business_model.customer_type: B2B -- global banks, asset managers, hedge funds, corporates, broker-dealers and regulators; no meaningful B2C exposure
business_model.geographic_mix: Global footprint across 170+ countries with operations in 60+; historically roughly Americas ~45%, EMEA ~35%, Asia-Pacific ~20% (Refinitiv/LSEG legacy mix), with GBP-reporting but meaningful USD and EUR revenue exposure

competitive_position.market_position: Top-three global player in essentially all of its major businesses; clear leader in real-time market data distribution (alongside Bloomberg and S&P), the number-one global clearer of interest rate swaps (SwapClear clears >90% of IRS notional cleared globally), a leading electronic fixed-income/rates trading venue (Tradeweb), and (via FTSE Russell) a top-three global index provider alongside S&P Dow Jones Indices and MSCI

moat_factors.factor: Scale and breadth of proprietary data
moat_factors.description: Over 33 petabytes of trusted, proprietary, non-replicable historical data with ~15-26 million new datapoints added per second (real-time network traffic grew 29% YoY to a peak of 26 million messages/second in June 2026); breadth across asset classes is difficult to replicate

LCH/SwapClear and Tradeweb benefit from liquidity network effects -- the largest pool of counterparties and dealers attracts further flow, reinforcing dominant share in cleared IRS and electronic fixed income trading

Deep workflow embedding (Workspace, Eikon-successor terminal used by hundreds of thousands of financial professionals) and long-term enterprise-wide Data Access Agreements create high switching costs; FTSE Russell index licensing is embedded in trillions of dollars of benchmarked AUM and fund mandates
LCH is a systemically important central counterparty regulated across multiple jurisdictions, acting as a quasi-regulatory barrier to new entrants in clearing
LSEG/Refinitiv/FTSE Russell/LCH are long-established, trusted brands in financial markets infrastructure, now being leveraged into an 'LSEG Everywhere' AI-data distribution strategy

Unlike vertically-integrated rivals, LSEG pursues interoperability (e.g., multi-cloud distribution via AWS, Azure, Google; MCP partnerships with Anthropic, OpenAI, Snowflake, Databricks), which broadens distribution reach but also lowers barriers for disintermediation

weaknesses: Data & Analytics (~42% of revenue) still carries legacy Refinitiv/Eikon-era products and is the segment most exposed to generative-AI/LLM disintermediation risk, with monetisation of new AI products still unproven
Workspace/Workflows organic growth (+3.1% FY2025) lags the rest of the group, suggesting continued competitive and pricing pressure from Bloomberg and newer AI-native data tools

Complexity of a multi-division conglomerate (data, indices, screening, trading venues, clearing) makes it harder for investors to value versus more focused peers (MSCI, ICE, S&P Global), a key driver of the Elliott Management activist campaign
FTSE Russell asset-based fees are correlated to equity market levels/AUM, introducing some market-beta sensitivity despite overall recurring characterisation
High financial leverage (operating net debt/EBITDA ~2.1x at June 2026, versus a 1.5-2.5x target range) constrains flexibility relative to less-levered index/ratings peers

growth_drivers: LSEG Everywhere AI data-distribution strategy: licensing proprietary data into AI workflows via Model Context Protocol (MCP), with partnerships across Microsoft Copilot Studio, Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI/ChatGPT, Amazon Quick, Google Gemini, Snowflake and Databricks; over 200 customers engaged on MCP server access as of H1 2026, with a developing commercial framework of recurring AI-data subscriptions, MCP access fees and premium Workspace AI tiers (AI Search: 17,000 active users; Deep Research: 7,000 users)
Strategic ten-year Microsoft partnership (Azure migration, Workspace/Teams/Copilot integration, joint Digital Markets Infrastructure build) driving both cost efficiency and new product delivery

Post Trade Solutions expansion into the large uncleared OTC derivatives market (comparable in size to the cleared segment), following the 2025 sale of a 20% stake to 11 global banks and extended SwapClear revenue-share economics through 2045

Digital assets / tokenisation: Digital Markets Infrastructure (DMI) platform (built with Microsoft/Azure), first private-fund and gilt tokenisation transactions, new LSE 24 digital/algorithmic trading venue (launching H1 2027), and the HSBC Digital Securities Depository/DIGIT collaboration for the UK's first digital gilt
New capital-markets venues: Private Securities Market (PISCES-approved, first operator) opening intermittent liquidity for private companies, expanding the 'funding continuum'
FTSE Russell private-markets and ESG index expansion (StepStone partnership, FTSE Blossom ESG series, Russell 9000 global index series, semi-annual Russell US reconstitution)
Continued double-digit growth in Risk Intelligence (Digital Identity & Fraud, World-Check On Demand/Verify) riding secular AML/KYC/fraud-prevention tailwinds
Structural electronification of fixed income and FX trading, benefiting Tradeweb and FXall/FX Matching

Margin expansion program: medium-term guidance of ~150bps cumulative adjusted EBITDA margin improvement 2027-2029 plus declining capex intensity (c.8% of total income by 2029), driving strong equity free cash flow growth (double-digit FCF/share CAGR targeted)
Continued large-scale capital returns (progressive dividend plus ongoing buybacks, over GBP 8bn cumulative since 2022 once the current programme completes) supporting EPS growth

business.risk: Generative AI / LLM disintermediation of data business
business.description: Data & Analytics (~42% of group revenue) is the segment most exposed to the risk that AI tools and large language models reduce demand for, or compress pricing of, traditional data terminals and feeds; monetisation of LSEG's own AI products remains unproven and this narrative has driven sharp share-price swings in 2026 (a ~13% one-day fall in February 2026 on AI-disruption fears)
Organic growth in Workflows (Workspace, the Eikon successor) has lagged other divisions (+3.1% FY2025), reflecting ongoing competitive pressure from Bloomberg and newer entrants

Company-identified emerging risk: AI, cloud computing, quantum computing and distributed ledger technology could lower barriers to entry and challenge core centralized-infrastructure services (flagged as an emerging risk in the FY2025 annual report)
Concurrent major change programmes -- platform/product upgrades, cloud migration, Microsoft partnership delivery, and ongoing integration following Refinitiv -- create execution and disruption risk
Increasing integration across divisions raises single-incident reputational contagion risk; limited IP protection could allow competitors to replicate products

financial.description: Operating net debt/adjusted EBITDA of 2.1x at June 2026 (target range 1.5-2.5x, intended to run around the midpoint), elevated versus the FY2025 year-end 1.8x, constraining capital-return flexibility at the margin

GBP-reporting group with substantial USD and EUR revenue; FX translation was a 1.5% reported-growth headwind in H1 2026 (GBP:USD 1.318, GBP:EUR 1.168 average rates); FX moves also affect reported EBITDA margin (60bps favourable FX benefit noted in H1 2026)
Through LCH, LSEG bears financial and operational risk from clearing member defaults, requiring the CCP to manage market/liquidity risk while restoring a matched book

regulatory.description: Diverse and evolving regulation across jurisdictions covering market access, market competitiveness, data localisation and financial crime compliance

LCH operates as a systemically important, heavily regulated central counterparty (CFTC, Bank of England, ESMA); rule changes (e.g., SwapClear fee/limit changes, WIBOR/LIBOR-style benchmark transitions) require constant regulatory filings and adaptation
Evolving rules on data usage rights, AI model governance and sustainability disclosure (CSRD) increase compliance costs and could affect commercial terms for AI-data licensing

macro.description: Conflicts (Ukraine, Middle East), US-China relations and protectionist trade policy could reduce transaction volumes and revenues, though the company notes volatility often benefits trading/clearing volumes, providing a partial natural hedge
FTSE Russell asset-based fees (34% of that division's revenue) are linked to ETF AUM and market levels, creating some beta to broad market performance
Net Treasury Income (NTI) earned on cash margin/default funds at LCH is sensitive to short-term interest rates; NTI organic revenue declined -2.6% in FY2025 on lower collateral balances

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Structural, secular growth in demand for data-driven decision-making, electronification/digitalisation of trading, rising regulatory/compliance burden, and capital optimisation needs; management characterises all of LSEG's addressable markets as growing at least mid-single-digit annually or better
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate -- over 70% recurring/subscription revenue provides defensiveness, while the ~30% transactional revenue (largely Tradeweb and post-trade/clearing) is positively correlated with market volatility, providing a partial natural hedge against a pure economic downturn
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity; modest exposure via LCH Net Treasury Income on cash collateral and via net finance costs on the Group's debt
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud infrastructure and third-party IT services
Staff costs (largest single cost line; ~28% of total income ex-recoveries in H1 2026)

recent_developments.event: LCH Group minority buy-in: LSEG agreed in July 2026 to acquire two minority shareholders' stakes (up to 1.05% combined) in LCH Group for EUR 70 million, taking LSEG's ownership of LCH Group to over 95%

Interim results (H1 2026): record first-half performance -- total income ex-recoveries organic growth +8.4%, adjusted EBITDA +14.1% with margin up 320bps to 52.7%, adjusted EPS +17.2% to 244.9p; 2026 full-year guidance raised (organic income growth to 7.0-7.5%, EBITDA margin improvement to ~100bps); GBP2.1bn in H1 buybacks completed with a further GBP1.35bn planned by February 2027; shares reportedly slipped despite the beat, as growth guidance remained below some analyst expectations and the Markets-led beat was seen as less durable

New venue and digital-asset announcements: launch of LSE 24 (a planned 24/5 digital/algorithmic/agentic trading venue, to launch H1 2027) and an MOU with HSBC for a Digital Securities Depository link supporting the UK's first digital gilt issuance (DIGIT), targeted by Q1 2027

AI-disruption narrative evolved through 2026: shares fell sharply (~13% in a single day) in February 2026 on fears that generative AI/LLMs would erode LSEG's data business; by mid-2026 sentiment partially recovered (UBS removed LSEG from its AI-disruption risk basket, arguing AI is a net positive), though a subsequent broker warning in July 2026 reignited concerns about monetisation timing (UBS expects AI monetisation to begin materially in 2027)

Activist investor Elliott Management disclosed a significant stake in LSEG, pushing for a larger buyback, portfolio/strategy review, margin improvement versus peers, and clearer communication on AI strategy; Elliott has told the UK government it does not seek a break-up or spin-off of the London Stock Exchange; LSEG's FY2025 results (Feb 2026) response included a GBP3bn buyback programme and raised margin guidance, which Elliott called a 'positive first start' while continuing to push for further value-unlocking steps

FY2025 full-year results: total income ex-recoveries organic growth +7.1%, adjusted EBITDA margin +210bps to 50.3%, adjusted EPS +15.7% to 420.6p, equity free cash flow GBP2.4bn, full-year dividend +15.4% to 150.0p, GBP2.1bn of FY2025 buybacks (GBP4.6bn cumulative since 2022); Eikon fully retired and ~350,000 users migrated to Workspace

Post Trade Solutions transaction: 11 leading global banks acquired a 20% stake in LSEG's Post Trade Solutions business for GBP170m (valuing PTS at GBP850m); SwapClear revenue-share agreement renegotiated, increasing LSEG's economics and extending the partner banks' reduced revenue share to 2045, contributing a one-off ~140bps H1 2026 EBITDA margin benefit that reverses in Q4 2026

Deepened Microsoft partnership: Workspace Office Add-ins, Workspace app in Teams, MCP infrastructure launch (Dec 2025) enabling customer AI agents via Microsoft Copilot Studio; multi-cloud AI-data distribution partnerships added with Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (ChatGPT), Snowflake and Databricks

Board changes: Lloyd Pitchford and Dame Elizabeth Corley joined the Board as Non-Executive Directors; Dominic Blakemore and Martin Brand to step down following the April 2026 AGM; Chris Coleman appointed Head of Sales and Account Management (Jan 2026), succeeding Ron Lefferts, who became Co-Head of Data & Analytics alongside new hire Gianluca Biagini (ex-S&P Global)

items.notes: Follows a record GBP2.1bn repurchased in H1 2026 (23.4m shares at average GBP88.39); would take cumulative buybacks since 2022 to over GBP8bn

guidance.management_commentary: CEO David Schwimmer characterised H1 2026 as a record first half, citing accelerating subscription growth, an exceptional first half for Markets (double-digit growth), and growing AI monetisation potential underpinned by LSEG's trusted data, regulatory expertise and institutional history. Management emphasised that growth in subscription businesses is accelerating and that customers see LSEG's solutions as 'more valuable in an AI world, not less,' while acknowledging that AI monetisation (recurring AI-data subscriptions, MCP access fees, premium Workspace AI tiers) is still in early commercial stages. Leverage was 2.1x at June 2026 (within the 1.5-2.5x target range, running above the midpoint), and management reiterated confidence in the 2026 guidance range, noting that the H1 EBITDA margin beat partly reflects a one-off SwapClear revenue-share benefit that will reverse in Q4 2026.

bull_case: Highly diversified, recurring (>70%) revenue base with genuine secular tailwinds (data/AI adoption, electronification, regulation, capital optimisation) across all four divisions, each growing organically mid-to-high single digits or better

Clear top-three (often number-one) competitive positions with durable moats in systemically important infrastructure (LCH/SwapClear clearing >90% of global cleared IRS notional, Tradeweb's leading electronic fixed-income platform, FTSE Russell's top-three index franchise)

AI is increasingly viewed by sell-side analysts (e.g., UBS) as a net positive rather than purely a threat, with LSEG's proprietary, auditable, regulatory-grade data seen as complementary to (not replaceable by) generative AI tools; early monetisation via MCP, Copilot Studio, Workspace AI Search/Deep Research is scaling quickly (200+ MCP customers, 17,000 AI Search users)

Accelerating margin expansion and declining capex intensity are driving strong, growing equity free cash flow (guided at least GBP2.7bn for FY2026, targeting double-digit FCF/share CAGR 2027-2029), funding both a progressive dividend (17% CAGR over 20 years) and very large ongoing buybacks (over GBP8bn cumulative since 2022 once current programme completes)

Activist investor Elliott Management's involvement increases the probability of further capital discipline, portfolio simplification and management accountability, which could help close any valuation gap versus peers such as S&P Global, MSCI and ICE
bear_case: Generative AI and LLM-native data/analytics tools pose a genuine long-term disintermediation threat to the Data & Analytics division (c.42% of revenue), and 2026 has already seen two sharp, AI-driven share-price selloffs; monetisation of LSEG's own AI offerings is unproven and management itself flags it as an emerging risk

H1 2026 earnings showed a pattern of guidance raised but still below some analyst expectations, with growth increasingly reliant on the more volatile, trading-volume-linked Markets division rather than structurally higher-quality subscription growth -- a pattern that could reverse if volatility subsides

Reported EBITDA margin improvement is partly inflated by one-off/non-recurring items (e.g., the SwapClear revenue-share change contributing ~140bps in H1 2026 that reverses in Q4), making the underlying organic margin trajectory harder to assess and raising questions about the durability of the 'all-weather' growth and margin story

Leverage (2.1x operating net debt/EBITDA, above the FY2025 year-end level and the midpoint it intends to run at) combined with very large ongoing capital returns leaves less room to absorb a shock or fund M&A without equity/debt market support

Complex, multi-segment conglomerate structure continues to attract activist pressure (Elliott Management) over an unresolved valuation gap to more focused data/index peers, and there is no guarantee management's current strategy -- rather than a more radical restructuring -- will close that gap
